questions.questionTextEn:
Select the word that is most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to the given word:
LACONIC
questions.explanationEn: 'LACONIC' means lasting for a very short time or being terse. The most appropriate synonym is 'TERSE'.
questions.questionTextHi:
दिए गए शब्द के सबसे निकटतम समानार्थक (SIMILAR) शब्द का चयन करें:
LACONIC
questions.explanationHi: 'LACONIC' का अर्थ 'संक्षिप्त / मितभाषी' होता है। इसका सही समानार्थक 'TERSE' है।

questions.questionTextEn:
Choose the grammatically correct option to fill in the blank:
She is proficient ______ both theoretical and experimental physics.
questions.explanationEn: 'Proficient in' a subject or field is standard English usage. Correct option is 'in'.
questions.questionTextHi:
रिक्त स्थान की पूर्ति के लिए व्याकरण की दृष्टि से सही विकल्प चुनें:
She is proficient ______ both theoretical and experimental physics.
questions.explanationHi: सही विकल्प 'in' है। 'Proficient in' a subject or field is standard English usage.

questions.questionTextEn: A man walks at $4\text{ km/h}$ and reaches his office 5 minutes late. If he walks at $5\text{ km/h}$, he reaches on time. The distance to his office in km is ______ (answer in integer).
questions.questionTextHi: A man walks at $4\text{ km/h}$ and reaches his office 5 minutes late. If he walks at $5\text{ km/h}$, he reaches on time. The distance to his office in km is ______ (answer in integer).

questions.questionTextEn:
Passage:
'Supercomputing simulations do not supersede laboratory experiments; rather, they provide computational experiments that explore parameter regimes inaccessible to current physical probes, guiding experimental design.'
Simulations are primarily valuable because they:
optionsEn: Probe extreme or inaccessible regimes and guide physical experiments
Cost nothing compared to physical devices

questions.questionTextEn: A card is drawn from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. The probability that it is either a king or a spade is:
questions.explanationEn: 4 kings + 13 spades - 1 (king of spades) = 16 cards. P = 16/52 = 4/13.
questions.questionTextHi: A card is drawn from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. The probability that it is either a king or a spade is:
questions.explanationHi: 4 kings + 13 spades - 1 (king of spades) = 16 cards. P = 16/52 = 4/13.

questions.questionTextEn: A clock loses 5 minutes per day. If it is set correctly at 12:00 noon on Monday, what time will it display at 12:00 noon on the following Monday (after 7 days)?
questions.explanationEn: Loses 5 * 7 = 35 minutes -> 12:00 - 35 min = 11:25 AM.
questions.questionTextHi: A clock loses 5 minutes per day. If it is set correctly at 12:00 noon on Monday, what time will it display at 12:00 noon on the following Monday (after 7 days)?
questions.explanationHi: Loses 5 * 7 = 35 minutes -> 12:00 - 35 min = 11:25 AM.

questions.questionTextEn: The diagonals of a rhombus are $16\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$. The area of the rhombus in $\text{cm}^2$ is ______ (answer in integer).
questions.questionTextHi: The diagonals of a rhombus are $16\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$. The area of the rhombus in $\text{cm}^2$ is ______ (answer in integer).

questions.questionTextEn: A cone and a cylinder have equal base radii and equal heights. The ratio of the volume of the cylinder to that of the cone is ______ (answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Vol cylinder = pi r^2 h. Vol cone = (1/3) pi r^2 h. Ratio = 3.
questions.questionTextHi: A cone and a cylinder have equal base radii and equal heights. The ratio of the volume of the cylinder to that of the cone is ______ (answer in integer).
questions.explanationHi: Vol cylinder = pi r^2 h. Vol cone = (1/3) pi r^2 h. Ratio = 3.

questions.questionTextEn: A lock-in amplifier operating at reference frequency $f_0 = 1\text{ kHz}$ with low-pass filter time constant $\tau = 1\text{ s}$ has an effective noise bandwidth of approximately:
questions.explanationEn: For an RC low-pass filter, the equivalent noise bandwidth is $B_n = \frac{1}{4\tau} = \frac{1}{4(1)} = 0.25\text{ Hz}$, allowing extreme noise rejection.
questions.questionTextHi: A lock-in amplifier operating at reference frequency $f_0 = 1\text{ kHz}$ with low-pass filter time constant $\tau = 1\text{ s}$ has an effective noise bandwidth of approximately:
questions.explanationHi: For an RC low-pass filter, the equivalent noise bandwidth is $B_n = \frac{1}{4\tau} = \frac{1}{4(1)} = 0.25\text{ Hz}$, allowing extreme noise rejection.

questions.questionTextEn: Under a coordinate transformation $x'^i = a^i_j x^j$, a rank-2 covariant tensor $T_{ij}$ transforms as:
questions.explanationEn: Covariant tensor indices transform with inverse partial derivatives: $T'_{ij} = \frac{\partial x^k}{\partial x'^i} \frac{\partial x^l}{\partial x'^j} T_{kl}$.
questions.questionTextHi: निर्देशांक रूपांतरण के अंतर्गत कोटि-2 सहपरिवर्ती (कोवेरिएंट) टेंसर $T_{ij}$ का रूपांतरण नियम क्या है?
questions.explanationHi: सहपरिवर्ती टेंसर सूचकांक आंशिक अवकलजों के व्युत्क्रम से रूपांतरित होते हैं: $T'_{ij} = \frac{\partial x^k}{\partial x'^i} \frac{\partial x^l}{\partial x'^j} T_{kl}$।

questions.questionTextEn: The residue of the function $f(z) = \frac{\cos z}{z^3}$ at the pole $z = 0$ is:
questions.explanationEn: Expanding $\cos z = 1 - \frac{z^2}{2!} + \frac{z^4}{4!} - \dots$, we have $f(z) = \frac{1}{z^3} - \frac{1}{2z} + \frac{z}{24} - \dots$. The coefficient of $1/z$ is $-1/2$.
questions.questionTextHi: ध्रुव $z = 0$ पर फलन $f(z) = \frac{\cos z}{z^3}$ का अवशेष क्या है?

questions.questionTextEn: A particle moves in a circular orbit under an attractive central force $F(r) = -k/r^2$. The ratio of its kinetic energy $T$ to its potential energy $V(r) = -k/r$ is:
questions.explanationEn: By the Virial theorem for $V(r) \propto r^n$ with $n = -1$: $2\langle T \rangle = n \langle V \rangle = -\langle V \rangle \implies T = -\frac{1}{2} V$. Hence $T/V = -1/2$.
questions.questionTextHi: केंद्रीय बल $F(r) = -k/r^2$ में वृत्ताकार कक्षा में गतिमान कण के लिए गतिज ऊर्जा $T$ और स्थितिज ऊर्जा $V$ का अनुपात क्या है?
questions.explanationHi: विरियल प्रमेय से $2T = -V \implies T/V = -1/2$।

questions.questionTextEn: The Poisson bracket between angular momentum component $L_x$ and linear momentum component $p_y$ is:
questions.questionTextHi: कोणीय संवेग घटक $L_x$ और रेखीय संवेग घटक $p_y$ के बीच प्वासों कोष्ठक का मान क्या है?

questions.questionTextEn: The electromagnetic wave equation in terms of the magnetic vector potential $\mathbf{A}$ in Lorenz gauge $\nabla \cdot \mathbf{A} + \frac{1}{c^2} \frac{\partial V}{\partial t} = 0$ in vacuum with current density $\mathbf{J}$ is:
questions.explanationEn: In Lorenz gauge, Maxwell's curl equations decouple into the inhomogeneous wave equation $\nabla^2 \mathbf{A} - \frac{1}{c^2} \frac{\partial^2 \mathbf{A}}{\partial t^2} = -\mu_0 \mathbf{J}$.
questions.questionTextHi: लॉरेंज गेज में चुंबकीय सदिश विभव $\mathbf{A}$ के लिए तरंग समीकरण क्या है?
questions.explanationHi: लॉरेंज गेज में $\nabla^2 \mathbf{A} - \frac{1}{c^2} \frac{\partial^2 \mathbf{A}}{\partial t^2} = -\mu_0 \mathbf{J}$।

questions.questionTextEn: For an electromagnetic wave propagating inside a hollow rectangular waveguide of width $a$, the phase velocity $v_p$ and group velocity $v_g$ satisfy:
questions.explanationEn: In waveguides with dispersion $\omega^2 = c^2 k^2 + \omega_c^2$, $v_p = \omega/k$ and $v_g = d\omega/dk$, leading directly to $v_p v_g = c^2$.
questions.questionTextHi: आयताकार वेवगाइड में कला वेग $v_p$ तथा समूह वेग $v_g$ में क्या संबंध है?

questions.questionTextEn: For a quantum particle in a one-dimensional delta-function potential well $V(x) = -\alpha \delta(x)$ with $\alpha > 0$, the bound-state energy is:
questions.explanationEn: Integrating the Schrödinger equation across $x = 0$ gives discontinuity $\Delta\psi' = -\frac{2m\alpha}{\hbar^2} \psi(0) \implies \kappa = \frac{m\alpha}{\hbar^2}$. Then $E = -\frac{\hbar^2 \kappa^2}{2m} = -\frac{m\alpha^2}{2\hbar^2}$.
questions.questionTextHi: एक-विमीय डेल्टा-फलन विभव $V(x) = -\alpha \delta(x)$ ($\alpha > 0$) में बद्ध अवस्था की ऊर्जा क्या है?
questions.explanationHi: $E = -\frac{m\alpha^2}{2\hbar^2}$।

questions.questionTextEn: For a particle confined in a two-dimensional symmetric square box of side $L$ with infinite walls, the energy of state $(n_x, n_y)$ is $E = \frac{\pi^2 \hbar^2}{2m L^2} (n_x^2 + n_y^2)$. The degeneracy of the first excited energy level is:
questions.explanationEn: The ground state is $(1, 1)$ (non-degenerate). The first excited level has $n_x^2 + n_y^2 = 1^2 + 2^2 = 5$, achieved by two states: $(1, 2)$ and $(2, 1)$, giving a degeneracy of 2.
questions.questionTextHi: द्वि-विमीय सममित वर्गाकार बॉक्स में प्रथम उत्तेजित ऊर्जा स्तर की अपभ्रष्टता (डीजेनेरेसी) क्या है?
questions.explanationHi: अवस्थाएँ $(1, 2)$ तथा $(2, 1)$ समान ऊर्जा $5 \frac{\pi^2 \hbar^2}{2mL^2}$ रखती हैं, अतः अपभ्रष्टता 2 है।

questions.questionTextEn: In a diffraction grating with grating element $(a + b)$ and $N$ total rulings, the chromatic resolving power $\lambda / \Delta \lambda$ in the $m$-th diffraction order is:
questions.explanationEn: The chromatic resolving power of a diffraction grating is given by $R = \frac{\lambda}{\Delta \lambda} = m N$.
questions.questionTextHi: In a diffraction grating with grating element $(a + b)$ and $N$ total rulings, the chromatic resolving power $\lambda / \Delta \lambda$ in the $m$-th diffraction order is:
questions.explanationHi: The chromatic resolving power of a diffraction grating is given by $R = \frac{\lambda}{\Delta \lambda} = m N$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a double-slit Fraunhofer diffraction pattern, if the slit width is $a$ and slit separation is $d$, the condition for missing orders (absent spectra) is:
questions.explanationEn: Missing orders occur when an interference maximum coincides with a diffraction minimum: $d \sin \theta = m \lambda$ and $a \sin \theta = p \lambda \implies m = p (d/a)$. For this to occur, $d/a$ must be an integer ratio.
questions.questionTextHi: द्वि-स्लिट विवर्तन में लुप्त कोटियों (मिसिंग ऑर्डर्स) के लिए शर्त क्या है?
questions.explanationHi: $d/a$ का मान एक पूर्णांक होना चाहिए।

questions.questionTextEn: For an ideal Fermi gas at temperature $T \ll T_F$, the electronic specific heat $C_V$ is proportional to:
questions.explanationEn: Only electrons within $k_B T$ of the Fermi level are thermally excited, so $C_V = \frac{\pi^2}{2} N k_B \left(\frac{T}{T_F}\right) \propto T$.
questions.questionTextHi: $T \ll T_F$ पर आदर्श फर्मी गैस की इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विशिष्ट ऊष्मा $C_V$ किसके समानुपाती होती है?
questions.explanationHi: $C_V \propto T$।

questions.questionTextEn: In a 3D ideal Bose gas below the condensation temperature ($T < T_c$), the chemical potential $\mu$ is identically:
questions.explanationEn: Macroscopic occupation of the single-particle ground state ($E = 0$) in the thermodynamic limit forces $\mu = 0$ for $T < T_c$.
questions.questionTextHi: 3D आदर्श बोस गैस में $T < T_c$ पर रासायनिक विभव $\mu$ क्या होता है?
questions.explanationHi: संक्रमण ताप से नीचे रासायनिक विभव $\mu = 0$ होता है।

questions.questionTextEn: In Mössbauer spectroscopy, recoil-free emission and absorption of $\gamma$-rays is made possible because:
optionsEn: The nucleus is isolated in free space
The gamma-ray energy is completely zero
The recoil momentum is absorbed by the crystal lattice as a whole, making recoil energy negligibly small
Temperature is maintained at absolute zero
questions.explanationEn: When bound in a crystal lattice, the entire macroscopic crystal ($M \gg m_{\text{nucleus}}$) absorbs the recoil momentum, making the recoil kinetic energy $E_R = \frac{p^2}{2M_{\text{crystal}}} \approx 0$.
questions.questionTextHi: मेसबॉअर स्पेक्ट्रोस्कोपी में $\gamma$-किरणों का प्रतिक्षेप-मुक्त (रिकॉइल-फ्री) उत्सर्जन कैसे संभव होता है?
optionsHi: नाभिक मुक्त आकाश में स्थित होता है
गामा किरण ऊर्जा शून्य होती है
प्रतिक्षेप संवेग पूरे क्रिस्टल जालक द्वारा अवशोषित होता है जिससे प्रतिक्षेप ऊर्जा नगण्य हो जाती है
questions.explanationHi: प्रतिक्षेप ऊर्जा पूरे क्रिस्टल जालक द्वारा वहन की जाती है, जिससे $E_R \approx 0$ होता है।

questions.questionTextEn: The Paschen-Back effect occurs when the external magnetic field is so strong that:
optionsEn: Spin-orbit coupling is stronger than the magnetic interaction
The magnetic interaction dominates over the spin-orbit coupling, uncoupling $\mathbf{L}$ and $\mathbf{S}$
questions.explanationEn: In the Paschen-Back effect, the strong magnetic field uncouples $\mathbf{L}$ and $\mathbf{S}$, so $m_l$ and $m_s$ become good quantum numbers instead of $j$ and $m_j$.
questions.questionTextHi: पाशन-बैक प्रभाव कब उत्पन्न होता है?
optionsHi: बाह्य चुंबकीय क्षेत्र इतना प्रबल हो कि $\mathbf{L}$ और $\mathbf{S}$ का युग्मन टूट जाता है
questions.explanationHi: प्रबल चुंबकीय क्षेत्र में $\mathbf{L}$ और $\mathbf{S}$ अलग-अलग $B$ के परितः पुरःसरण करते हैं।

questions.questionTextEn: In an ideal metal-semiconductor contact (n-type semiconductor with work function $\Phi_s$ and metal with work function $\Phi_m$), a rectifying Schottky barrier is formed when:
questions.explanationEn: For an n-type semiconductor, a rectifying Schottky barrier requires $\Phi_m > \Phi_s$ so that electrons flow from semiconductor to metal until equilibrium band bending creates a barrier $\Phi_B = \Phi_m - \chi$.
questions.questionTextHi: धातु-अर्धचालक संपर्क (n-प्रकार) में दिष्टकारी शोट्की रोधिका कब बनती है?
questions.explanationHi: n-प्रकार अर्धचालक के लिए शोट्की रोधिका हेतु $\Phi_m > \Phi_s$ आवश्यक है।

questions.questionTextEn: In an intrinsic semiconductor, the Fermi level $E_F$ is located at:
optionsEn: The top of the valence band
Approximately in the middle of the bandgap: $E_F = \frac{E_c + E_v}{2} + \frac{3}{4} k_B T \ln(m_h^* / m_e^*)$
The bottom of the conduction band
Directly at the donor energy level
questions.explanationEn: From carrier statistics $n = p$, $E_F = \frac{E_c + E_v}{2} + \frac{3}{4} k_B T \ln(m_h^* / m_e^*)$, which lies very close to the center of the bandgap.
questions.questionTextHi: नैज अर्धचालक में फर्मी स्तर $E_F$ कहाँ स्थित होता है?
optionsHi: लगभग बैंड अंतराल के मध्य में
questions.explanationHi: नैज अर्धचालक में $E_F$ बैंड अंतराल के ठीक मध्य के समीप होता है।

questions.questionTextEn: An astable multivibrator constructed using an operational amplifier with positive feedback operates as:
optionsEn: A free-running relaxation oscillator producing a square waveform
questions.explanationEn: An op-amp astable multivibrator switches between positive and negative saturation voltages as a timing capacitor charges and discharges through a resistor, producing a continuous square wave.
questions.questionTextHi: ऑप-एम्प द्वारा निर्मित अस्टेबल मल्टीवाइब्रेटर किस रूप में कार्य करता है?
optionsHi: वर्गाकार तरंग उत्पन्न करने वाले मुक्त दोलक के रूप में
questions.explanationHi: यह निरंतर वर्गाकार तरंग उत्पन्न करने वाला रिलैक्सेशन दोलक है।

questions.questionTextEn: A Schmitt trigger circuit uses which type of feedback to create hysteresis?
questions.explanationEn: Positive feedback applied to the non-inverting terminal creates two distinct threshold voltages ($V_{UT}$ and $V_{LT}$), producing hysteresis.
questions.questionTextHi: श्मिट ट्रिगर परिपथ में हिस्टैरिसीस उत्पन्न करने के लिए किस प्रकार का पुनर्निवेश उपयोग किया जाता है?
questions.explanationHi: अ-प्रतिलोमी टर्मिनल पर धनात्मक पुनर्निवेश से हिस्टैरिसीस उत्पन्न होता है।

questions.questionTextEn: In the Weizsäcker semi-empirical mass formula, the asymmetry energy term proportional to $(A - 2Z)^2 / A$ arises due to:
optionsEn: The Pauli exclusion principle acting differently when proton and neutron numbers differ
questions.explanationEn: Protons and neutrons occupy separate Fermi levels. Any difference $(N - Z) = A - 2Z$ forces nucleons to occupy higher kinetic energy states, reducing binding energy.
questions.questionTextHi: अर्ध-आनुभविक द्रव्यमान सूत्र में असममिति ऊर्जा पद $(A - 2Z)^2/A$ का मूल कारण क्या है?
questions.explanationHi: प्रोटॉन और न्यूट्रॉन के अलग-अलग फर्मी स्तरों में भरने पर पाउली सिद्धांत के कारण ऊर्जा में वृद्धि होती है।

questions.questionTextEn: The quark structure of the neutral pion $\pi^0$ is represented by the superposition:
questions.explanationEn: The neutral pion is the $I = 1, I_3 = 0$ member of the pseudoscalar meson octet, described by $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} (u \bar{u} - d \bar{d})$.
questions.questionTextHi: उदासीन पायन $\pi^0$ की क्वार्क संरचना क्या है?
questions.explanationHi: $\pi^0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} (u \bar{u} - d \bar{d})$।

questions.questionTextEn: A quantity $Z = X^2 Y^{1/2}$ is calculated from independent measurements. If the percentage uncertainty in $X$ is $2.0\%$ and in $Y$ is $6.0\%$, the percentage standard uncertainty in $Z$ is ______\% (answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Relative uncertainty: $(\Delta Z / Z)^2 = (2 \Delta X / X)^2 + (0.5 \Delta Y / Y)^2 = (2 \times 1.5)^2 + (0.5 \times 4.0)^2 = 3.0^2 + 2.0^2 = 9 + 4 = 13 \implies \Delta Z/Z = \sqrt{13} \approx 3.61\%$. Wait, if $\Delta X / X = 1.5\%$ and $\Delta Y / Y = 4\%$, let's set $\Delta X / X = 1.5\%, \Delta Y / Y = 4\%$ -> $3^2 + 2^2 = 13$. For integer: if $\Delta X/X = 1.5\%$ and $\Delta Y/Y = 4.0\%$, $\sqrt{13} \approx 3.6$. If $\Delta X / X = 1.5\%$ and $\Delta Y/Y = 4.0\%$, let's set $\Delta X/X = 1.5\%$ with $(2 \times 1.5) = 3$ and $0.5 \times 4 = 2$. What if $\Delta X/X = 1.5\%$ and $\Delta Y/Y = 4\%$? What if $(\Delta Z/Z) = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5\%$ with $\Delta Y/Y = 8\%$? Let $\Delta X/X = 2\%$ and $\Delta Y/Y = 6\%$: $(2 \times 2)^2 + (0.5 \times 6)^2 = 4^2 + 3^2 = 25 \implies 5\%$! Let's use $5\%$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a double-slit interference experiment, the distance between the two slits is $d = 0.8\text{ mm}$ and the width of each slit is $a = 0.2\text{ mm}$. The ratio $d/a$ which determines the missing order of interference is ______ (answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: $d/a = 0.8 / 0.2 = 4$. Thus, the 4th, 8th, 12th ... interference maxima are missing.
questions.questionTextHi: द्वि-स्लिट प्रयोग में $d = 0.8\text{ mm}$ तथा $a = 0.2\text{ mm}$ के लिए अनुपात $d/a$ ______ है।

questions.questionTextEn: For an electron in a hydrogen atom in the state with principal quantum number $n = 3$, the total orbital spatial degeneracy (summing over all allowed orbital states $\sum_{l=0}^{n-1} (2l+1)$, excluding spin) is ______ (answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Degeneracy without spin is $n^2 = 3^2 = 9$.
questions.questionTextHi: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु में $n = 3$ स्तर के लिए कुल कक्षीय अपभ्रष्टता (चक्रण रहित) ______ है।

questions.questionTextEn: In a full-wave bridge rectifier operating from a $50\text{ Hz}$ AC power line, the fundamental ripple frequency in the rectified DC output in Hz is ______ (answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: For full-wave rectification, the ripple frequency is twice the input AC line frequency: $f_{\text{ripple}} = 2 f_{\text{line}} = 2 \times 50\text{ Hz} = 100\text{ Hz}$. Wait, let's make the answer 100 Hz or adjust text: ripple frequency is 100 Hz.
questions.questionTextHi: $50\text{ Hz}$ प्रत्यावर्ती लाइन से संचालित पूर्ण-तरंग दिष्टकारी के निर्गत में रिपल आवृत्ति ______ Hz होती है।
questions.explanationHi: $f_{\text{ripple}} = 2 \times 50 = 100\text{ Hz}$।

questions.questionTextEn: In a lock-in amplifier, an input signal $V_{\text{in}}(t) = V_s \cos(\omega_s t + \phi) + V_n(t)$ where $V_n(t)$ is broad-band noise, is multiplied by a square-wave reference signal $V_{\text{ref}}(t)$ of fundamental frequency $\omega_r$. If $\omega_s = \omega_r$ and the phase difference is adjusted to $\phi = 0$, the DC output from the low-pass filter with unity gain is proportional to:
questions.explanationEn: Multiplying $\cos(\omega_r t) \times \cos(\omega_r t) = \frac{1}{2}[1 + \cos(2\omega_r t)]$. The low-pass filter eliminates the AC $2\omega_r$ component and all noise at $\omega \ne \omega_r$, leaving a pure DC output proportional to $V_s$.

questions.explanationHi: Multiplying $\cos(\omega_r t) \times \cos(\omega_r t) = \frac{1}{2}[1 + \cos(2\omega_r t)]$. The low-pass filter eliminates the AC $2\omega_r$ component and all noise at $\omega \ne \omega_r$, leaving a pure DC output proportional to $V_s$.

questions.questionTextEn: The value of the contour integral $\oint_{|z|=2} \frac{z^3 + 1}{(z - 1)^2 (z + 3)} \, dz$ evaluated counterclockwise along the circle $|z| = 2$ in the complex plane is:
questions.explanationEn: Only the double pole at $z = 1$ lies inside $|z| = 2$. By Cauchy's Residue Theorem, $\text{Res}(f, 1) = \lim_{z \to 1} \frac{d}{dz}\left[\frac{z^3 + 1}{z + 3}\right] = \left. \frac{3z^2(z+3) - (z^3+1)}{(z+3)^2} \right|_{z=1} = \frac{12 - 2}{16} = \frac{5}{8}$. Thus, $\oint = 2\pi i (5/8) = \frac{5\pi i}{4}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A one-dimensional quantum harmonic oscillator of mass $m$ and frequency $\omega$ is perturbed by $H' = \lambda x^4$. Using first-order time-independent perturbation theory, the shift in the ground state energy is:
questions.explanationEn: For the ground state of a harmonic oscillator, $\langle x^4 \rangle_0 = 3 \langle x^2 \rangle_0^2 = 3 \left(\frac{\hbar}{2m\omega}\right)^2 = \frac{3\hbar^2}{4m^2\omega^2}$. Hence $\Delta E_0^{(1)} = \frac{3\lambda\hbar^2}{4m^2\omega^2}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Which of the following statements regarding experimental measurements and error analysis is/are CORRECT?
(A) The four-probe method eliminates contact resistance by measuring voltage across probes that carry virtually zero current.
(B) Random errors can be reduced by averaging multiple independent measurements, whereas systematic errors cannot.
(C) Single-point star grounding helps eliminate ground loops by preventing circulating noise currents.
(D) The ripple factor of a full-wave rectifier is independent of load resistance $R_L$.
optionsEn: The four-probe method eliminates contact resistance by measuring voltage across probes that carry virtually zero current.
Random errors can be reduced by averaging multiple independent measurements, whereas systematic errors cannot.
Single-point star grounding helps eliminate ground loops by preventing circulating noise currents.
The ripple factor of a full-wave rectifier is independent of load resistance $R_L$.
questions.explanationEn: A, B, C are correct. D is false because ripple factor $r \propto 1/(R_L C)$.

Which of the following statements regarding optical polarization and interference is/are CORRECT?
(A) A quarter-wave plate converts linearly polarized light at $45^\circ$ to its optic axis into circularly polarized light.
(B) In a Fabry-Pérot interferometer, higher mirror reflectivity $R$ leads to higher coefficient of finesse and narrower transmission peaks.
(C) At Brewster's angle, the reflected and refracted beams are mutually perpendicular.
(D) The Jones vector $\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$ represents vertically polarized light.
optionsEn: A quarter-wave plate converts linearly polarized light at $45^\circ$ to its optic axis into circularly polarized light.
In a Fabry-Pérot interferometer, higher mirror reflectivity $R$ leads to higher coefficient of finesse and narrower transmission peaks.
At Brewster's angle, the reflected and refracted beams are mutually perpendicular.
The Jones vector $\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$ represents vertically polarized light.
questions.explanationEn: A, B, C are correct. D is false because $\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$ represents horizontally polarized light.

questions.questionTextEn:
A classical particle of mass $m$ moves in a central potential $V(r) = -k/r$ ($k > 0$). Which of the following quantities is/are conserved during its motion?
(A) Total mechanical energy $E$
(B) Total angular momentum vector $\mathbf{L}$
(C) Laplace-Runge-Lenz vector $\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{p} \times \mathbf{L} - m k \hat{\mathbf{r}}$
(D) Linear momentum vector $\mathbf{p}$
questions.explanationEn: A, B, C are strictly conserved in a $1/r$ central potential. Linear momentum is not conserved due to the central force.
questions.questionTextHi:

(A) Total mechanical energy $E$

(C) Laplace-Runge-Lenz vector $\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{p} \times \mathbf{L} - m k \hat{\mathbf{r}}$
(D) Linear momentum vector $\mathbf{p}$
questions.explanationHi: A, B, C are strictly conserved in a $1/r$ central potential. Linear momentum is not conserved due to the central force.

questions.questionTextEn:
Which of the following statements about quantum mechanical systems is/are CORRECT?
(A) For a particle in an infinite 1D square well, the energy levels satisfy $E_n \propto n^2$.
(B) A 1D attractive delta-function potential $V(x) = -\alpha \delta(x)$ ($\alpha > 0$) has exactly one bound state.
(C) The ground state of a 1D harmonic oscillator minimizes the Heisenberg uncertainty product $\Delta x \, \Delta p = \hbar/2$.
(D) The parity of the spherical harmonic $Y_l^m(\theta, \phi)$ under spatial inversion is $(-1)^m$.
optionsEn: For a particle in an infinite 1D square well, the energy levels satisfy $E_n \propto n^2$.
A 1D attractive delta-function potential has exactly one bound state.
The ground state of a 1D harmonic oscillator minimizes the Heisenberg uncertainty product $\Delta x \, \Delta p = \hbar/2$.
The parity of the spherical harmonic $Y_l^m(\theta, \phi)$ under spatial inversion is $(-1)^m$.
questions.explanationEn: A, B, C are true. D is false because parity is $(-1)^l$, determined by orbital quantum number $l$, not $m$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Which of the following statements regarding superconductors and semiconductors is/are CORRECT?
(A) Below the critical field $H_c$, a Type-I superconductor expels magnetic flux completely (Meissner effect).
(B) In a superconductor, the London penetration depth $\lambda_L$ is given by $\sqrt{\frac{m}{\mu_0 n_s e^2}}$.
(C) For an intrinsic semiconductor, the electrical conductivity increases exponentially with temperature.
(D) In an n-type semiconductor, the Fermi level moves closer to the conduction band as donor doping concentration increases.
optionsEn: Below the critical field $H_c$, a Type-I superconductor expels magnetic flux completely (Meissner effect).
In a superconductor, the London penetration depth $\lambda_L$ is given by $\sqrt{\frac{m}{\mu_0 n_s e^2}}$.
For an intrinsic semiconductor, the electrical conductivity increases exponentially with temperature.
In an n-type semiconductor, the Fermi level moves closer to the conduction band as donor doping concentration increases.
questions.explanationEn: All four statements (A, B, C, D) are exact physical facts.

questions.questionTextEn: A particle of mass $m$ is in an attractive delta-function potential well $V(x) = -\alpha \delta(x)$ in 1D. If the binding energy of the state is $E_b = 2.0\text{ eV}$, and the strength $\alpha$ is doubled to $2\alpha$, the new binding energy in eV is ______ (answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Bound state energy $E_b = \frac{m \alpha^2}{2\hbar^2} \propto \alpha^2$. Doubling $\alpha$ quadruples the binding energy: $2.0 \times 4 = 8.0\text{ eV}$.

questions.questionTextHi: In a Michelson interferometer, when the movable mirror is displaced by $150\,\mu\text{m}$, 500 interference fringes cross the field of view. The wavelength of the light in nanometers is ______ (answer in integer).
questions.explanationHi: $2 \Delta d = N \lambda \implies \lambda = \frac{2(150 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m})}{500} = 600 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m} = 600\text{ nm}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A spherical blackbody of radius $R_1 = 10\text{ cm}$ at temperature $T_1 = 2000\text{ K}$ radiates power $P_1$. A second blackbody of the same radius at $T_2 = 1000\text{ K}$ radiates power $P_2$. The ratio $P_1 / P_2$ is ______ (answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: By Stefan-Boltzmann law, $P \propto T^4$. $P_1 / P_2 = (2000/1000)^4 = 2^4 = 16$.
questions.questionTextHi: A spherical blackbody of radius $R_1 = 10\text{ cm}$ at temperature $T_1 = 2000\text{ K}$ radiates power $P_1$. A second blackbody of the same radius at $T_2 = 1000\text{ K}$ radiates power $P_2$. The ratio $P_1 / P_2$ is ______ (answer in integer).
questions.explanationHi: By Stefan-Boltzmann law, $P \propto T^4$. $P_1 / P_2 = (2000/1000)^4 = 2^4 = 16$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a singly ionized helium atom ($\text{He}^+, Z = 2$), the excitation energy required to transition an electron from $n = 1$ to $n = 2$ in eV (rounded off to one decimal place, taking Rydberg energy $= 13.6\text{ eV}$) is ______.
questions.explanationEn: $\Delta E = 13.6 \times Z^2 (1 - 1/4) = 13.6 \times 4 \times (3/4) = 40.8\text{ eV}$.
questions.questionTextHi: In a singly ionized helium atom ($\text{He}^+, Z = 2$), the excitation energy required to transition an electron from $n = 1$ to $n = 2$ in eV (rounded off to one decimal place, taking Rydberg energy $= 13.6\text{ eV}$) is ______.
questions.explanationHi: $\Delta E = 13.6 \times Z^2 (1 - 1/4) = 13.6 \times 4 \times (3/4) = 40.8\text{ eV}$.
